proof:
# Exact three-root funding with one equal central pair

This note excludes a specific remaining tetrahedral weighted-capacity configuration: a global maximum chosen with the fewest nonzero rows, with three full rows and a common section centroid

    b=(a,c,B,B),  a>1/3, c>1/3, B>0, a+c+2B=1.

The first two coordinates need not agree. The proof uses the three actual stationary roots, rather than convexity of a stiffness function between them. It does not classify a completely nonsymmetric centroid, a centroid with only one noncentral coordinate, or Oertel's conjecture.

The capacity is phi_3(x)=inf_{t>0} t/Pr(x dot Xi<=t)^(1/3), where Xi is uniform on the probability tetrahedron. The three positive rows form a column-stochastic matrix; its fourth row is zero. Objective weights are strictly positive. The previously proved positive-row regularity theorem, the minimal-active rank theorem, the common-section-centroid stationarity equations, and the joint-positive-index theorem are used in precisely their stated scopes.

## 1. Actual section structure and three distinct roots

At a putative global maximum chosen with the fewest nonzero rows, all full rows have proper, unique, nondegenerate minimizing cuts. Their section centroids equal b after normalizing the common column multiplier sum to one. Their actual raw margin vectors sum to zero. The three active rows are linearly independent.

Since two coordinates of b exceed 1/3, the same-side noncentral theorem and the triangular-section centroid formulas imply that every section is a strict quadrilateral with unoriented split {1,2}|{3,4}. Equality and centrality of b_3=b_4=B force the corresponding two raw margin heights to be equal. Here is the applicable diagonal argument. Normalize reciprocal diagonal coordinates (x,y,z,w) to sum one, put r=xy, s=zw, and D0=(x+z)(x+w)(y+z)(y+w). The actual section formula gives

    3(b_3-b_4)=(z-w)[r-(r-s)^2]/D0.

The two centrality inequalities are (s-r)z<=r and (s-r)w<=r. If r>=s, then (r-s)^2<r, since r<=1/4. If s>r and (s-r)^2>=r, the larger of z,w is at least sqrt(s), giving (s-r)max(z,w)>=sqrt(rs)>r, a contradiction. Thus the bracket is positive and z=w. Reciprocal normalization proves equality of the two raw heights.

Orient every section toward the first pair and choose its representative

    C(p)=(p,q,-1,-1), p,q>0.

Because the plane passes through b,

    a p+c q=2B,  q=(2B-a p)/c.                     (1)

Put D=a-c, so a=(1-2B+D)/2 and c=(1-2B-D)/2. Define

    U=1/(1+p), V=1/(1+q), T=2-U-V.

Direct quadrilateral integration gives

    3a=U(1+T-U)/T,  3c=V(1+T-V)/T,                (2)
    P=1-UV(3-U-V),  f=UVT.

Here P is the captured tetrahedral fraction and f the density at zero of the exponential raw-margin sum. In particular T>0. Substituting (1) in the first equation (2) and clearing its positive denominators gives the cubic F(p)=0, where

    F(p)=3(2B-D-1)^2 p^3
      +6(6B^2-5BD-3B+D^2+D)p^2
      +(36B^2-24BD-8B+3D^2+1)p
      +2B(6B-3D-1).                                (3)

Every actual section is among these roots. There are three distinct actual sections: if two raw margins were proportional, their sum-zero relation would make all three proportional, and the active rows would belong to span{1,C}, contrary to rank three. Consequently (3), whose leading coefficient is 12a^2>0, has exactly their three distinct roots p_1<p_2<p_3. Each associated q_i is positive.

## 2. Exact interpolation of reciprocal stiffness

Let e=(0,0,1,-1). For the representative C(p), set

    J(p)=e^T Hess(P)(C(p)) e/(3f).

The central-pair cap-curvature theorem, applied to the complementary cap, gives J(p)>0 at each actual section. Direct differentiation and (2) give the more explicit formula

    J(p)=2B-4BT+(2/3)T^2.                           (4)

Before using stationarity, the corresponding expression is

    2[(U+V-1)^3+UV(3-2U-2V)]/[3(2-U-V)].

The stationary identities UV=T^2-(1+3B)T+1 and (4B-T)(2T-1)^2=3D^2T reduce it to (4); the polynomial argument below also applies when T=1/2, since no division by 2T-1 is made.

Although 1/J need not be convex on all positive p,q, its three stationary values agree with a strictly convex quadratic. Define

    E=432B^2D^2-216BD^2-8B+27D^4+18D^2+3,
    L=2B-D-1,

    N2=-9L^2(4B-3D^2-1),
    N1=-18L(24B^2D+8B^2-6BD^2-12BD-2B+3D^3+D),
    N0=-3(288B^3D+48B^3-180B^2D^2-144B^2D-12B^2
            +36BD^3+96BD^2+12BD-9D^4-6D^2-1).

Then, at every actual root of (3),

    1/J(p) = G(p):=(N2 p^2+N1 p+N0)/(2BE).          (5)

This is an exact polynomial identity, not an interpolation assumption. To check it, substitute q=(2B-a p)/c, U=(1+p)^(-1), V=(1+q)^(-1) and T=2-U-V in (4); multiply J(p)G(p)-1 by its denominators. Division by the explicit cubic (3) has zero remainder. Equivalently, if J=N_J/D_J is written in reduced rational form, the polynomial N_J(N2 p^2+N1 p+N0)-2BE D_J is divisible by F. The displayed coefficients specify every term of this identity. None of the denominators vanishes at an actual root: c,p+1,q+1,T,J are positive, and E is positive as follows.

We have 0<B<1/6 and |D|<1/3. On 0<=B<=1/6,

    24B^2-12B+1>=-1/3.

Therefore

    E=27D^4+18(24B^2-12B+1)D^2+3-8B
      >=3-8B-6D^2>1.                              (6)

Also 4B-3D^2-1<0 and L=-2a!=0. Hence N2/(2BE)>0, proving the asserted strict convexity of G.

If theta=(p_3-p_2)/(p_3-p_1), then 0<theta<1 and the exact quadratic identity reads

    theta/J(p_1)+(1-theta)/J(p_3)-1/J(p_2)
      =[N2/(2BE)](p_2-p_1)(p_3-p_2)>0.             (7)

## 3. Orientation, scaling, and actual stochastic funding

Represent the actual raw margins by signed multiples of C(p_i). Their sum is zero. The last coordinate gives that the three signed coefficients sum to zero; the first gives their p-weighted sum zero. Since the p_i are ordered, the two outer coefficients have one sign and the middle coefficient the opposite sign. If the outer coefficients are negative, both outer rows capture the two central coordinates 3,4. Each has a positive capacity direction, contradicting the joint-index bound k+sum positive indices<=4 at k=3. Thus the only potentially maximizing orientation is

    c_1=lambda_1 C(p_1),
    c_2=-lambda_2 C(p_2),
    c_3=lambda_3 C(p_3),                            (8)

with all lambda_i>0 and

    lambda_2=lambda_1+lambda_3,
    lambda_1/lambda_2=theta.                        (9)

Normalize the objective so that its full-row weights are P_i^(1/3), where P_i is the actually oriented cap fraction. Equal raw coordinates 3,4 make the threshold Schur correction along e exactly zero. The weighted capacity curvatures at the ACTUAL rows are consequently

    -J(p_1)/lambda_1,
    +J(p_2)/lambda_2,
    -J(p_3)/lambda_3,                               (10)

respectively. The change of sign in the middle row is because it is the complementary cap; its section density is unchanged by orientation reversal. Scaling raw margins by lambda scales this weighted curvature by 1/lambda. Thus (10) has the correct original stochastic-row units.

Give row 2 the direction e and give rows 1,3 the directions -u e and -(1-u)e. Leave the identically zero fourth row unchanged. The column sums are exactly preserved; all full entries stay positive for both signs of a sufficiently small parameter. The common gradient b gives zero first derivative. The maximum second derivative over u is

    J(p_2)/lambda_2
      -1/[lambda_1/J(p_1)+lambda_3/J(p_3)].          (11)

Indeed minimizing A u^2+C(1-u)^2 gives AC/(A+C), with A=J(p_1)/lambda_1 and C=J(p_3)/lambda_3. By (7) and (9),

    lambda_1/J(p_1)+lambda_3/J(p_3)>lambda_2/J(p_2),

so (11) is strictly positive. This is an actual feasible improving second variation, contradicting local maximality.

The conclusion is therefore exact: a tetrahedral weighted-capacity global maximizer chosen with the fewest nonzero rows with three full rows cannot have a common section centroid (a,c,B,B) with a,c>1/3. No deformation to this centroid pattern, and no all-centroid classification, is asserted.

The final argument is local once row independence is supplied: any stationary configuration with three independent full rows and these centroid coordinates has the explicit improving path above. Minimality among global maximizers is used only to guarantee that independence. No independence theorem for arbitrary support-minimal local maxima is used.
